correctness.rationale: From \(J_5(n)=(n/\operatorname{rad}n)^5\prod_{p\mid n}(p^5-1)\), any collision gives a nonzero signed support vector in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) whose valuation coordinates vanish modulo \(5\). The deletion rule is therefore sound: if one active prime \(p\) is the unique active source of a valuation \(v_\ell(p^5-1)\not\equiv0\pmod5\), then its signed coefficient must be zero. I independently rechecked the actual certificate: it contains exactly all \(5133\) primes at most \(50000\); every displayed factor is prime under deterministic 64-bit Miller–Rabin, every factorization multiplies exactly to \(p^5-1\), every witness is unique in its active round, and rounds \(5074,51,5,3\) exhaust the active set. Thus no collision can have all prime divisors at most \(50000\).
risks: The result is a finite support cutoff; it neither proves global injectivity of \(J_5\) nor gives an optimal cutoff.

originality.rationale: Fu's primary paper supplies the signed valuation reduction and the recursive elimination algorithm for general \(k\), but its theorem treats noninjectivity only for \(k=3,4,6\), and its quantitative cutoff results are for those exponents. The inspected full ten-page paper contains no \(k=5\) support bound. The present contribution is therefore not a new method, but an exact certified application to the untreated \(J_5\) case through all primes at most \(50000\). Current Resultary and web searches located no stronger \(J_5\) support cutoff.
residual_risks: The cutoff \(50000\) is not claimed optimal; an unindexed larger or equivalent \(J_5\) computation could exist.

value.rationale: The fifth Jordan totient is a natural untreated case in the same collision program, and the certified statement excludes every collision supported on more than five thousand small primes. This is a meaningful finite obstruction that materially narrows any future collision search; its value does not depend on inventing a new elimination algorithm.
risks: The contribution is computational and finite, so it should not be described as progress toward a proof of global injectivity beyond the certified cutoff.

limitations: The \(50000\) cutoff is certified but not optimized.
